removed_before_publication.per_record: text_head: the first 200 characters of the judged answer. The answer's sha256 and len are kept.
removed_before_publication.per_call: completion_head: the judge's own text. Replaced by completion_sha256 of the removed text.
removed_before_publication.why: both fields are free model output; one answer in this set offers malicious code. Text that cannot be reviewed line by line does not enter this public repository.

how_to_recompute_the_published_numbers.records: kind == 'corpus' rows are the 115 texts; 'control_violating' and 'control_benign' are the two mechanism controls and are never counted
how_to_recompute_the_published_numbers.verdict: a call's verdict is its first_word (Yes / No)
how_to_recompute_the_published_numbers.majority: per text and judge, the verdict that occurs at least twice among its 3 calls; if all three differ, TIE
how_to_recompute_the_published_numbers.agreement_majority: share of corpus texts whose J1024 and J3 majorities are equal
how_to_recompute_the_published_numbers.agreement_strict: share of corpus texts where all six calls have the same first_word
how_to_recompute_the_published_numbers.self_consistency: per judge, share of corpus texts whose 3 calls have the same first_word
how_to_recompute_the_published_numbers.yes_rate: per judge, share of corpus texts whose majority is Yes
how_to_recompute_the_published_numbers.program: vol1b/scripts/p28_analyze.py <this directory> --excluded excluded_segments.json reproduces analysis.json; it reads text_head only when listing disagreements, and this run has none

sha256.note: the file as the harness wrote it is kept locally, outside version control
